 Petrol, Diesel Prices Today, October 27, 2026: Check Rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Other Cities

 Mumbai, October 27: Fuel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Tuesday. Petrol costs Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi and Rs 111.21 in Mumbai, while diesel is priced at Rs 95.20 per litre in Delhi and Rs 97.83 in Mumbai. Among the listed cities, Hyderabad has the highest petrol price at Rs 116.15 per litre, while Thiruvananthapuram records the highest diesel rate at Rs 104.40.   
 Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday, October 27, as renewed diplomatic efforts to ease the US-Israeli war on Iran raised hopes of reduced supply disruptions. However, continued attacks on Saudi Arabia kept crude benchmarks near six-month highs, limiting the decline. Brent crude futures fell 0.96% to $114.7 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 0.9% to $100.8 per barrel.   
 Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to establish channels for negotiations and prevent further military escalation. The countries agreed to continue discussions on peace and security, fuelling hopes of easing regional tensions.   
 However, the diplomatic efforts have yet to eliminate concerns over energy supplies. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis have claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s East-West crude oil pipeline pumping stations and Riyadh airport, while the Saudi-led coalition said it had destroyed drones targeting Riyadh and other areas. The conflict has also disrupted commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, key routes for global energy trade.   
 Brent crude climbed about 6% last week, while WTI gained 2.3%, as attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping heightened fears of supply disruptions. With geopolitical risks persisting, investors remain cautious about whether the latest price retreat will be sustained. For oil-importing countries such as India, crude prices hovering around $115 per barrel pose risks to inflation, the import bill and corporate profitability.   
 Check the latest petrol and diesel prices in Delhi, Noida, Gurgaon, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru and other cities.   
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Tuesday, with New Delhi recording a rate of Rs 102.12 per litre. In neighbouring Gurgaon, petrol was priced at Rs 102.97 per litre, while Noida had a lower rate of Rs 101.96 per litre. Chandigarh recorded a price of Rs 101.54 per litre.   
 Among the major metropolitan cities, petrol retailed at Rs 113.51 per litre in Kolkata, Rs 111.21 in Mumbai and Rs 107.76 in Chennai. Bangalore recorded a price of Rs 111.68 per litre, while Bhubaneswar had a rate of Rs 108.97 per litre.   
 Petrol prices were higher in several other state capitals. Hyderabad recorded the highest rate among the listed cities at Rs 116.15 per litre, followed by Thiruvananthapuram at Rs 115.49. Jaipur’s petrol price stood at Rs 113.19 per litre, while Patna recorded Rs 113.37 per litre.   
 In Lucknow, petrol was priced at Rs 101.86 per litre. There was no change in petrol prices across any of the 14 listed cities, with rates remaining steady compared with the previous update. Prices vary across states and cities due to differences in local taxes, including value-added tax (VAT), and transportation costs.    
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Tuesday, with the fuel retailing at Rs 95.20 per litre in New Delhi. In neighbouring Gurgaon, diesel was priced at Rs 95.64 per litre, while Noida recorded a rate of Rs 95.44 per litre. Chandigarh had a considerably lower price of Rs 89.47 per litre, the cheapest among the listed cities.   
 Among the major metropolitan centres, diesel was priced at Rs 99.82 per litre in Kolkata, Rs 97.83 in Mumbai and Rs 99.55 in Chennai. Bangalore recorded a rate of Rs 99.56 per litre, while Bhubaneswar’s diesel price stood at Rs 100.68 per litre.   
 Hyderabad and Thiruvananthapuram recorded the highest diesel prices among the listed cities, at Rs 104.23 and Rs 104.40 per litre, respectively. In other state capitals, diesel retailed at Rs 98.25 per litre in Jaipur and Rs 99.36 in Patna.   
 In Lucknow, diesel was priced at Rs 95.36 per litre, with no change reported across any of the 13 cities listed. Retail prices vary across states and cities due to differences in local taxes, including value-added tax (VAT), and transportation costs.
